{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZhf1Og", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDIelg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 65, "title": "Correct Mode 7 screen-row origin for BG1 and EXTBG sampling", "body": "## Problem

Mode 7 currently treats the first framebuffer row as screen Y=0. The scheduler renders physical scanlines 1–224 into framebuffer rows 0–223, but `Ppu::mode7` consumes the framebuffer row directly, including before vertical flipping. See [scheduler conversion](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a321b4b757cae117a8241be614a6a954b00f53b0/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L192) and [Mode 7 sampling](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a321b4b757cae117a8241be614a6a954b00f53b0/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L542).

The [Issue #63 validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a321b4b757cae117a8241be614a6a954b00f53b0/docs/issue-63-validation.md#L68) explicitly records that Fullsnes starts SCREEN.Y at 1 and leaves this discrepancy unresolved. Its CPU-built transform guests set B=D=0, making their output independent of screen Y. Existing direct pixel tests instead encode the retained zero-based convention. Passing those tests does not resolve the coordinate contract.

This is the incomplete behavior prioritized by the latest assessment. It is distinct from #63's completed displacement-clipping and product-truncation corrections. The supplied context lists no open Issues.

## Expected outcome

Reconcile the documented screen coordinate with the scheduler's framebuffer coordinate, then implement the supported conversion once in the shared static Mode 7 sampling path. BG1 and EXTBG BG2 must sample the same transformed byte using the resolved screen Y.

### Specification contract

The repository's [recorded specification reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a321b4b757cae117a8241be614a6a954b00f53b0/docs/issue-63-validation.md#L17) cites:

- [Fullsnes: SNES PPU Rotation/Scaling](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesppurotationscaling), including SCREEN.Y, M7SEL flips and separately truncated origin products.
- [Anomie's Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), revision 1157: $211A, $211B–$2120 and BACKGROUNDS / Mode 7, covering flips, signed inputs, clipping, fixed-point products and shared EXTBG sampling.

The expected documentary correction, subject to passage-level reconciliation before implementation, is:

```text
r = framebuffer row, 0..223
screen_y = r + 1
xf = HFLIP ? (x XOR 255) : x
yf = VFLIP ? (screen_y XOR 255) : screen_y

clip(v) = (v & 1023) - (1024 if v & 8192 else 0)
T(v) = v & ~63
dh = clip(s13(HOFS) - s13(CX))
dv = clip(s13(VOFS) - s13(CY))
PX = (T(A*dh) + T(B*dv) + T(B*yf) + 256*s13(CX) + A*xf) >> 8
PY = (T(C*dh) + T(D*dv) + T(D*yf) + 256*s13(CY) + C*xf) >> 8
```

A–D remain signed 16-bit 8.8 coefficients; shifts are arithmetic. Preserve #63's clipping, separate six-bit truncation, screen-over addressing and independent layer decoding. Convert the row before vertical flipping; flipping the framebuffer row and then adding one gives different results.

With identity A=D=256, B=C=0 and zero offsets/centers, candidate source Y values are:

| Framebuffer row | Current, normal | Expected, normal | Current, V-flipped | Expected, V-flipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 1 | 255 | 254 |
| 223 | 223 | 224 | 32 | 31 |

These are documentary expectations, not physical-console measurements. This read-only planning pass inspected repository evidence only; the previously retrieved specification copies are absent locally, and external sources were not reopened. Record the exact supporting passages and reconcile scanline terminology before changing production behavior. If that reconciliation disproves a candidate requirement, correct this contract and its vectors with evidence rather than preserving an unsupported historical expectation. Anomie's tentative arithmetic qualification and unresolved physical fetch timing must remain explicit.

### Scope and remaining work

Limit implementation to static, non-mosaic, non-interlaced, 256-pixel Mode 7 screen-row conversion, including BG1 and EXTBG BG2. Keep framebuffer indexing zero-based. Do not globally shift planar BGs, OBJ, windows, HDMA events or framebuffer storage.

Mode 7 remains partial. Mosaic, interlace/overscan, EXTBG with pseudo-hires, comprehensive transform/window/color-math interactions, multiplication latency/rendering interference, physical reset retention, mid-scanline writes and fetch/arbitration timing remain outside this Issue. Documentary row-origin agreement does not verify the physical rendering pipeline.

Retain every supplied inventory category and its complete existing scope and limitations. Statuses remain: partial — cpu, bus, scheduler, dma, hdma, controllers, ppu-bg, ppu-offset, ppu-hires, ppu-mode7, ppu-objects, ppu-color, ppu-ports, ppu-display, spc, ipl, dsp-noise, dsp-pitch, dsp-envelope, dsp-echo, dsp-timing; implemented_unverified — dsp-voices; unimplemented — ppu-raster, pal. No category becomes verified.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `a321b4b757cae117a8241be614a6a954b00f53b0`.

Extend the sparse, asymmetric scene approach in [ppu_mode7_transform.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a321b4b757cae117a8241be614a6a954b00f53b0/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_mode7_transform.rs). Place distinguishable source pixels on adjacent rows, render framebuffer rows 0 and 223, and compare literal expected colors for BG1-only and BG2-only routing. Identity D=256 exposes the current one-row difference; B-only vectors expose it independently in transformed X.

Also use signed/fractional B and D, nonzero offsets/centers and both vertical-flip states. For example, under the candidate contract, A=128, B=64, C=-64, D=128, HOFS=5, VOFS=-3, CX=2, CY=-2 at framebuffer (7,9) samples (9,0), versus current (9,-1). With VFLIP it samples (68,117), versus current (68,118). Independently derive and document every committed expected coordinate.

Existing source references include [the CPU guest builder](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a321b4b757cae117a8241be614a6a954b00f53b0/crates/snes-core/tests/common/mode7_transform.rs) and [the browser observations](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a321b4b757cae117a8241be614a6a954b00f53b0/web/tests/mode7-transform.spec.js). No tests were executed during this planning pass.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the source passages, versions and coordinate interpretation supporting the resolved conversion and flip order. Explain which previous row-sensitive expectations are superseded and why. Implement the demonstrated correction; documentation or convention-only assertions do not complete this Issue.
- [ ] Add original public-API pixel regressions with literal source coordinates and RGBA expectations, independently derived from the reconciled specification. Cover first/last visible rows, an interior row, B-only and D-only dependence, positive/negative fractional coefficients, nonzero signed offsets/centers, VFLIP off/on and combined H/V flipping. Exercise BG1-only and EXTBG BG2-only routing. Artwork must distinguish adjacent and distant source coordinates rather than repeat indistinguishably.
- [ ] Demonstrate meaningful failures against the exact baseline using tests compatible with its public API. Include independent X and Y discriminators and flipped endpoint cases. Show the corrected implementation passing those same expectations. Expected pixels must not be calculated by production helpers or a runtime copy of the production transform.
- [ ] Reconcile affected #59/#61/#63 direct-test expectations individually. Preserve latch, clipping, truncation, screen-over, transparency, priority and direct-color coverage. Retain row-independent transform guest controls; do not compensate guest offsets merely to conceal an incorrect conversion.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built CPU guest, with BG1/BG2 and normal/V-flipped variants, that initializes under forced blank and uses nonzero B and D. Execute through the natural scheduler without host register or raster-state injection. Bound startup by instructions and frames, reject CPU/APU errors, discard the setup frame, and assert literal endpoint/interior pixels across at least three complete stable frames. Assert 256×224 geometry and 229376 RGBA bytes. Include a native runner PPM check of the distinguishing pixels.
- [ ] Run the same generated guest bytes through the browser's ordinary ROM picker. Assert completion, actual Wasm framebuffer pixels and canvas ImageData at first/last/interior rows, geometry and repeated observations. Reject console/page/core errors. Add the checks to the existing mandatory browser selection.
- [ ] Record original authorship, license, source/build commands and generated SHA-256 hashes in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`. Rebuild the new fixtures twice and compare bytes. Commit source only; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Also run `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_mode7_transform --test ppu_mode7_scroll --test ppu_mode7_extbg --test direct_color --test ppu_pseudo_hires --test ppu_obj_limits`, plus the new focused target if separate.
- [ ] Run the existing source-built hardware gates documented in README: `python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc`; `python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"`; and `python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"`. Preserve pinned sources, licensing and existing assertions.
- [ ] Run the original smoke-fixture reproducibility check, build the cleared games twice with `python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py`, then run `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build`, `(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)`, and `npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'`. Preserve Castle/Memory source pins, hashes, replay inputs, gameplay/audio assertions and test selection. Follow README toolchain prerequisites.
- [ ] Update README and a focused validation record with source reconciliation, baseline counterexamples, actual commands/results and remaining uncertainty. Preserve all 24 inventory scopes/statuses. Report failures and unperformed checks honestly; limited passes establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Physical-console measurements using the same original guest may strengthen the documentary conclusion, but are not required for merge.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
